dashboard.title: Dashboard
dashboard.howToDescription: This section contains basic documentation on how to use the extension.
howToList: To open content in isolation: Right-click on any link, image, or selected text and choose an option from the "SealSkin Isolation" context menu.
To send a download to isolation: Right-click on the page and select "Send Next Download to Isolation". The next file you download will be intercepted and sent to a secure session.
To launch a clean application: Click the SealSkin icon in your browser's toolbar.
To manage persistent storage: Use the "Home Directories" tab on this page to create and delete storage volumes that can be used across multiple sessions.

To save launch options: Check the "Save these launch options" box in the popup before launching an application for a specific file type (e.g., .pdf) or for all URLs. Manage these saved preferences in the "Pinned Behavior" tab.

SELKIES_UI_SHOW_LOGO.label: Show Logo
SELKIES_UI_SHOW_LOGO.description: Show the Selkies logo in the sidebar.

SELKIES_UI_SHOW_CORE_BUTTONS.label: Show Core Buttons
SELKIES_UI_SHOW_CORE_BUTTONS.description: Show the core components buttons (display, audio, etc).

SELKIES_UI_SIDEBAR_SHOW_VIDEO_SETTINGS.label: Show Video Settings
SELKIES_UI_SIDEBAR_SHOW_VIDEO_SETTINGS.description: Show the video settings section in the sidebar.

SELKIES_UI_SIDEBAR_SHOW_SCREEN_SETTINGS.label: Show Screen Settings
SELKIES_UI_SIDEBAR_SHOW_SCREEN_SETTINGS.description: Show the screen settings section in the sidebar.

SELKIES_UI_SIDEBAR_SHOW_AUDIO_SETTINGS.label: Show Audio Settings
SELKIES_UI_SIDEBAR_SHOW_AUDIO_SETTINGS.description: Show the audio settings section in the sidebar.

SELKIES_UI_SIDEBAR_SHOW_STATS.label: Show Stats
SELKIES_UI_SIDEBAR_SHOW_STATS.description: Show the stats section in the sidebar.

SELKIES_UI_SIDEBAR_SHOW_SHORTCUTS.label: Show Keyboard Shortcuts Section
SELKIES_UI_SIDEBAR_SHOW_SHORTCUTS.description: Show the keyboard shortcuts section in the sidebar.

SELKIES_UI_SIDEBAR_SHOW_CLIPBOARD.label: Show Clipboard
SELKIES_UI_SIDEBAR_SHOW_CLIPBOARD.description: Show the clipboard section in the sidebar.

SELKIES_UI_SIDEBAR_SHOW_FILES.label: Show Files Section
SELKIES_UI_SIDEBAR_SHOW_FILES.description: Show the file transfer section in the sidebar.

SELKIES_UI_SIDEBAR_SHOW_APPS.label: Show Apps Section
SELKIES_UI_SIDEBAR_SHOW_APPS.description: Show the applications section in the sidebar.

SELKIES_UI_SIDEBAR_SHOW_SHARING.label: Show Sharing Section
SELKIES_UI_SIDEBAR_SHOW_SHARING.description: Show the sharing section in the sidebar.

SELKIES_UI_SIDEBAR_SHOW_GAMEPADS.label: Show Gamepads Section
SELKIES_UI_SIDEBAR_SHOW_GAMEPADS.description: Show the gamepads section in the sidebar.

SELKIES_UI_SIDEBAR_SHOW_WEBCAM.label: Show Webcam Button
SELKIES_UI_SIDEBAR_SHOW_WEBCAM.description: Show the webcam toggle among the core buttons and stream controls. Hides the control only; Enable Webcam decides whether the server accepts camera frames.

SELKIES_UI_SIDEBAR_SHOW_FULLSCREEN.label: Show Fullscreen Button
SELKIES_UI_SIDEBAR_SHOW_FULLSCREEN.description: Show the fullscreen button in the sidebar.

SELKIES_UI_SIDEBAR_SHOW_GAMING_MODE.label: Show Gaming Mode Button
SELKIES_UI_SIDEBAR_SHOW_GAMING_MODE.description: Show the gaming mode (pointer lock) button in the sidebar.

SELKIES_UI_SIDEBAR_SHOW_TRACKPAD.label: Show Trackpad Button
SELKIES_UI_SIDEBAR_SHOW_TRACKPAD.description: Show the virtual trackpad button in the sidebar.

SELKIES_UI_SIDEBAR_SHOW_SOFT_BUTTONS.label: Show Soft Buttons
SELKIES_UI_SIDEBAR_SHOW_SOFT_BUTTONS.description: Show the soft buttons section (for mobile).

WATERMARK_PNG.label: Watermark PNG Path
WATERMARK_PNG.description: Full path inside the container to a watermark png.

WATERMARK_LOCATION.label: Watermark Location
WATERMARK_LOCATION.description: Where to paint the image over the stream.

DASHBOARD.label: Dashboard Style
DASHBOARD.description: Allows the user to set their dashboard.

SELKIES_MICROPHONE_ENABLED.label: Enable Microphone
SELKIES_MICROPHONE_ENABLED.description: Enable client-to-server microphone forwarding. Off by default upstream.

SELKIES_WEBCAM_ENABLED.label: Enable Webcam
SELKIES_WEBCAM_ENABLED.description: Forward the client's camera to the virtual webcam device. The base image turns it on when it creates the device; Disable Webcam Injection removes both.

SELKIES_ENABLE_CLIPBOARD.label: Clipboard Policy
SELKIES_ENABLE_CLIPBOARD.description: Which clipboard directions are allowed. 'Server to client only' also stops the page reading the local clipboard, which is what triggers paste prompts in Firefox and Safari.

SELKIES_ENABLE_BINARY_CLIPBOARD.label: Enable Binary Clipboard
SELKIES_ENABLE_BINARY_CLIPBOARD.description: Allow binary data (images) on the clipboard.

SELKIES_CLIPBOARD_SEAMLESS.label: Seamless Clipboard Sync
SELKIES_CLIPBOARD_SEAMLESS.description: Synchronize the clipboard as either side changes it, so a copy is ready to paste on the other. Off moves content only through the sidebar's clipboard box; the direction policy still applies.

SELKIES_COMMAND_ENABLED.label: Enable Command Websocket
SELKIES_COMMAND_ENABLED.description: Enable parsing of command websocket messages.

SELKIES_FILE_TRANSFERS.label: File Transfers
SELKIES_FILE_TRANSFERS.description: Allowed directions ('upload,download', 'upload', 'download', or 'none'). Emptied by Harden Desktop unless set here.

SELKIES_FILE_TRANSFER_LIMIT_MBPS.label: File Transfer Limit (Mbit/s)
SELKIES_FILE_TRANSFER_LIMIT_MBPS.description: Static throttle shared by all uploads and downloads. 0 disables the cap.

FILE_MANAGER_PATH.label: File Transfer Directory
FILE_MANAGER_PATH.description: Directory uploads land in and the file browser serves, created at start when missing.

SELKIES_PRINTING_ENABLED.label: Enable Printing
SELKIES_PRINTING_ENABLED.description: Hand documents printed to the session's Selkies queue to the browser as PDFs. Off refuses them and hides the printer section; Harden Desktop turns it off unless set here.

SELKIES_ENABLE_SHARING.label: Enable All Sharing
SELKIES_ENABLE_SHARING.description: Master toggle for all sharing features.

SELKIES_ENABLE_COLLAB.label: Enable Collaboration
SELKIES_ENABLE_COLLAB.description: Let a viewer holding the session's master token act as a read-write collaborator. Required for SealSkin rooms.

SELKIES_ENABLE_PLAYER2.label: Enable Player 2 Sharing
SELKIES_ENABLE_PLAYER2.description: Enable the sharing link for gamepad player 2.

SELKIES_ENABLE_PLAYER3.label: Enable Player 3 Sharing
SELKIES_ENABLE_PLAYER3.description: Enable the sharing link for gamepad player 3.

SELKIES_ENABLE_PLAYER4.label: Enable Player 4 Sharing
SELKIES_ENABLE_PLAYER4.description: Enable the sharing link for gamepad player 4.

SELKIES_SECOND_SCREEN.label: Enable Second Screen
SELKIES_SECOND_SCREEN.description: Enable support for a second monitor/display.

SELKIES_ENABLE_RESIZE.label: Enable Dynamic Resize
SELKIES_ENABLE_RESIZE.description: Resize the remote display to match the browser window.

SELKIES_USE_BROWSER_CURSORS.label: Use Browser Cursors
SELKIES_USE_BROWSER_CURSORS.description: Use browser CSS cursors instead of rendering to canvas.

SELKIES_ENABLE_CURSORS.label: Enable Remote Cursors
SELKIES_ENABLE_CURSORS.description: Send the application's own cursor shapes to the client.

SELKIES_CURSOR_SIZE.label: Cursor Size
SELKIES_CURSOR_SIZE.description: Cursor size in points at 96 DPI, scaled with the session DPI. -1 uses the platform default (32 on X11, 24 on Wayland).

SELKIES_KEYBOARD_SHORTCUTS.label: Client Keyboard Shortcuts
SELKIES_KEYBOARD_SHORTCUTS.description: Keep the client's own chords (Control+Shift with F, M, X, or G, and Control+Shift+click) instead of passing them to the session. Turn off where an application binds the same chords.

SELKIES_MAC_CMD_AS_CTRL.label: macOS Command as Control
SELKIES_MAC_CMD_AS_CTRL.description: Send a macOS client's Command chords as Control chords, so Cmd+C copies in the remote application. Turn off where the window manager binds Super; Command then arrives as Super.

SELKIES_RAW_POINTER_MOTION.label: Raw Pointer Motion
SELKIES_RAW_POINTER_MOTION.description: Ask the browser for unaccelerated pointer movement under pointer lock, so a locked pointer moves by the mouse's own counts. Windows and macOS grant it; Linux and Android keep their curve.

SELKIES_PUBLISH_INPUT_DEVICES.label: Publish Input Devices
SELKIES_PUBLISH_INPUT_DEVICES.description: Mirror the session keyboard and pointer onto input devices for applications that read evdev instead of the display server, such as fullscreen games and remappers. The desktop is driven as before.

SELKIES_UINPUT_GAMEPAD.label: Kernel Gamepad Devices
SELKIES_UINPUT_GAMEPAD.description: Register gamepads through /dev/uinput so Steam, Proton, and in-session browsers find them without the interposer. Auto does so only where the interposer is not configured and /dev/uinput is writable.

SELKIES_USE_CSS_SCALING.label: Use CSS Scaling (LoDPI)
SELKIES_USE_CSS_SCALING.description: If true, a lower resolution is sent and the canvas is stretched.

SELKIES_MANUAL_RESOLUTION.label: Manual Resolution Mode
SELKIES_MANUAL_RESOLUTION.description: Lock the resolution to the manual width/height values.

SELKIES_FORCE_ALIGNED_RESOLUTION.label: Force Aligned Resolution
SELKIES_FORCE_ALIGNED_RESOLUTION.description: Forces the display resolution to be a multiple of 16 pixels.

SELKIES_MANUAL_WIDTH.label: Manual Width
SELKIES_MANUAL_WIDTH.description: Lock width to a fixed value. Forces manual mode.

SELKIES_MANUAL_HEIGHT.label: Manual Height
SELKIES_MANUAL_HEIGHT.description: Lock height to a fixed value. Forces manual mode.

SELKIES_SCALING_DPI.label: UI Scaling DPI
SELKIES_SCALING_DPI.description: The default DPI for UI scaling.

SELKIES_VIDEO_ON_START.label: Video On at Start
SELKIES_VIDEO_ON_START.description: Start with the display's video stream on. Off captures nothing for the primary display until the client turns video on; shared viewers and second displays always start theirs.

SELKIES_AUDIO_ON_START.label: Audio On at Start
SELKIES_AUDIO_ON_START.description: Start with server-to-client audio on. Off leaves the capture stopped until the client turns audio on; unlike disabling audio, nothing is torn down and the microphone keeps working.

SELKIES_MICROPHONE_ON_START.label: Microphone Start Policy
SELKIES_MICROPHONE_ON_START.description: When the browser is asked for the microphone: at connect, when the sidebar toggle is used, or only while an application records from the virtual source.

SELKIES_WEBCAM_ON_START.label: Webcam Start Policy
SELKIES_WEBCAM_ON_START.description: When the browser is asked for the camera: at connect, when the sidebar toggle is used, or only while an application holds the virtual device open.

SELKIES_GAMEPAD_ON_START.label: Gamepads On at Start
SELKIES_GAMEPAD_ON_START.description: Start with gamepad input on. Off leaves connected gamepads unpolled until the client turns them on; the browser remembers that choice.

SELKIES_AUDIO_FRAME_DURATION_MS.label: Audio Frame Duration
SELKIES_AUDIO_FRAME_DURATION_MS.description: Opus frame duration. Lower values cut audio latency at a small bandwidth and packet-rate cost.

SELKIES_AUDIO_CHANNELS.label: Audio Channels
SELKIES_AUDIO_CHANNELS.description: Number of audio channels; 2 is stereo.

SELKIES_AUDIO_REDUNDANCY.label: Audio Redundancy (Opus RED)
SELKIES_AUDIO_REDUNDANCY.description: Carry prior audio frames as redundancy to cut dropouts under packet loss.

SELKIES_AUDIO_REDUNDANCY_DISTANCE.label: Audio Redundancy Distance
SELKIES_AUDIO_REDUNDANCY_DISTANCE.description: Number of prior frames carried as redundancy (0-4). Higher survives longer loss bursts at proportionally more bandwidth.

SELKIES_ENCODER.label: Encoders
SELKIES_ENCODER.description: Comma-separated list of allowed encoders: h264enc, h265enc, vp8enc, vp9enc, av1enc, h264enc-striped, jpeg. The first is the default and a single value locks the choice; clients step through the ones their browser decodes. WebRTC carries the full-frame encoders; h264enc-striped and jpeg are WebSocket-only.

SELKIES_FRAMERATE.label: Framerate (Range or Fixed)
SELKIES_FRAMERATE.description: e.g. '8-240' for a range, '60' for a fixed initial value, '60,8-240' for both; '60-60' locks it.

SELKIES_RATE_CONTROL_MODE.label: Rate Control Mode
SELKIES_RATE_CONTROL_MODE.description: Default rate control for the video encoders: constant quality (CRF) or constant bitrate (CBR).

SELKIES_ENABLE_RATE_CONTROL.label: Allow Rate Control Switching
SELKIES_ENABLE_RATE_CONTROL.description: Let clients switch between CRF and CBR. Off locks the encoder to its built-in default.

SELKIES_VIDEO_CRF.label: Video CRF (Range or Fixed)
SELKIES_VIDEO_CRF.description: Constant quality on the H.264 QP scale, mapped onto each codec: '5-50' for a range, '25' for a fixed initial value, or '25,5-50' for both.

SELKIES_VIDEO_BITRATE.label: Video Bitrate kbps (Range or Fixed)
SELKIES_VIDEO_BITRATE.description: CBR bitrate in kilobits per second: '100-1000000' for a range, '8000' for a fixed initial value, or '8000,100-1000000' for both.

SELKIES_VIDEO_MIN_QP.label: Video Minimum QP
SELKIES_VIDEO_MIN_QP.description: CBR-mode minimum H.264 quantizer (0 = encoder default). Raising it caps bit spend on easy content.

SELKIES_VIDEO_MAX_QP.label: Video Maximum QP
SELKIES_VIDEO_MAX_QP.description: CBR-mode maximum H.264 quantizer (0 = encoder default). Lowering it keeps text legible under motion at the cost of overshooting the bitrate target.

SELKIES_KEYFRAME_INTERVAL.label: Keyframe Interval (seconds)
SELKIES_KEYFRAME_INTERVAL.description: Seconds between scheduled recovery keyframes. 0 keeps the GOP infinite and sends keyframes only on demand.

SELKIES_JPEG_QUALITY.label: JPEG Quality (Range or Fixed)
SELKIES_JPEG_QUALITY.description: '1-100' for a range, '40' for a fixed initial value, or '40,1-100' for both.

SELKIES_VIDEO_FULLCOLOR.label: Video Full Color (4:4:4)
SELKIES_VIDEO_FULLCOLOR.description: Encode with 4:4:4 chroma where the codec and encoder carry it (H.264 and H.265 on NVENC, VA-API, x264, and x265; VP9 on VA-API and libvpx). A client without the 4:4:4 profile streams 4:2:0 on the same codec unless this is locked on, when it steps to the next encoder it decodes.

SELKIES_VIDEO_STREAMING_MODE.label: Video Streaming (Turbo) Mode
SELKIES_VIDEO_STREAMING_MODE.description: Encode every frame like a traditional video encoder instead of only changed regions.

SELKIES_USE_PAINT_OVER_QUALITY.label: Use Paint-Over Quality
SELKIES_USE_PAINT_OVER_QUALITY.description: Enable high-quality paint-over for static scenes.

SELKIES_PAINT_OVER_JPEG_QUALITY.label: Paint-Over JPEG Quality
SELKIES_PAINT_OVER_JPEG_QUALITY.description: '1-100' for a range, '90' for a fixed initial value, or '90,1-100' for both.

SELKIES_VIDEO_PAINTOVER_CRF.label: Paint-Over Video CRF
SELKIES_VIDEO_PAINTOVER_CRF.description: '5-50' for a range, '18' for a fixed initial value, or '18,5-50' for both.

SELKIES_VIDEO_PAINTOVER_BURST_FRAMES.label: Paint-Over Burst Frames
SELKIES_VIDEO_PAINTOVER_BURST_FRAMES.description: '1-30' for a range, '5' for a fixed initial value, or '5,1-30' for both.

SELKIES_BACKPRESSURE_QUEUE_SIZE.label: Backpressure Queue Size
SELKIES_BACKPRESSURE_QUEUE_SIZE.description: Frames and audio chunks buffered per stream before dropping under backpressure (WebSockets mode). Higher tolerates client hiccups at the cost of latency.

SELKIES_WEBCAM_WIDTH.label: Webcam Width
SELKIES_WEBCAM_WIDTH.description: Width of the virtual webcam device; client frames are scaled and letterboxed to fit.

SELKIES_WEBCAM_HEIGHT.label: Webcam Height
SELKIES_WEBCAM_HEIGHT.description: Height of the virtual webcam device; client frames are scaled and letterboxed to fit.

SELKIES_WEBCAM_ENCODER.label: Webcam Uplink Encoder
SELKIES_WEBCAM_ENCODER.description: Codec clients encode the camera uplink with. Auto runs the measured ladder: H.264, else VP8, then VP9, AV1, and H.265 where the browser encodes them, and JPEG when none keeps up. A codec name pins that codec, falling to JPEG where it cannot keep up.

SELKIES_WEBCAM_PIXEL_FORMAT.label: Webcam Pixel Format
SELKIES_WEBCAM_PIXEL_FORMAT.description: Pixel format of the virtual webcam device. Auto follows what the client sends.

HARDEN_DESKTOP.label: Harden Desktop (Preset)
HARDEN_DESKTOP.description: Enables DISABLE_OPEN_TOOLS, DISABLE_SUDO, and DISABLE_TERMINALS, and unless set explicitly also disables file transfers, the command websocket, printing, and the files and apps sidebar sections. Forced on for users with Harden Container.

HARDEN_OPENBOX.label: Harden Window Manager (Preset)
HARDEN_OPENBOX.description: Enables DISABLE_CLOSE_BUTTON, DISABLE_MOUSE_BUTTONS, and HARDEN_KEYBINDS for Openbox and labwc, and RESTART_APP unless set explicitly. Forced on for users with Harden Window Manager.

DISABLE_CLOSE_BUTTON.label: Disable Window Close Button
DISABLE_CLOSE_BUTTON.description: Removes the close button from window title bars.

DISABLE_MOUSE_BUTTONS.label: Disable Right/Middle Click
DISABLE_MOUSE_BUTTONS.description: Disables right-click and middle-click context menus.

HARDEN_KEYBINDS.label: Harden Keybinds
HARDEN_KEYBINDS.description: Disables window manager keybinds such as Alt+F4, Alt+Escape, Alt+Space, and Super+E, and locks the window manager config.

RESTART_APP.label: Restart App on Close
RESTART_APP.description: Automatically restarts the main application if it is closed and makes the autostart file read-only.

PIXELFLUX_WAYLAND.label: Wayland Backend
PIXELFLUX_WAYLAND.description: Run the session on the Wayland backend, a headless compositor with labwc nested for window management, instead of the X11 server. X11 applications run through XWayland.

MAX_RES.label: Maximum Resolution
MAX_RES.description: Max resolution for the container, default is 16k.

START_DOCKER.label: Start Docker-in-Docker
START_DOCKER.description: If false, a privileged container will not start DinD.

DISABLE_IPV6.label: Disable IPv6
DISABLE_IPV6.description: If true, this will disable IPv6.

DISABLE_ZINK.label: Disable Zink
DISABLE_ZINK.description: Do not set Zink env vars if a video card is detected.

DISABLE_DRI3.label: Disable DRI3
DISABLE_DRI3.description: Do not use DRI3 acceleration if a video card is detected.

AUTO_GPU.label: Automatic GPU Selection
AUTO_GPU.description: 'true' renders on the first GPU, 'false' disables it, or a vendor, driver, or PCI vendor ID (nvidia, amdgpu, 0x10de) picks a specific one.

DRI_NODE.label: Encode Render Node
DRI_NODE.description: DRI render node the video encoder uses (VA-API or NVENC), such as /dev/dri/renderD128. Empty follows Automatic GPU Selection.

DRINODE.label: Render Node
DRINODE.description: DRI render node the X server (DRI3) or the Wayland compositor renders on, such as /dev/dri/renderD128. Empty follows Automatic GPU Selection.

NO_DECOR.label: No Window Decorations
NO_DECOR.description: Run application without window borders for PWA use.

NO_GAMEPAD.label: Disable Gamepad Injection
NO_GAMEPAD.description: Skip the userspace gamepad interposer. Also hides the gamepad section and player sharing links.

NO_WEBCAM.label: Disable Webcam Injection
NO_WEBCAM.description: Skip the virtual webcam device and interposer. Also hides the webcam button.

NO_STEAM.label: Remove Steam Shim
NO_STEAM.description: Do not install the image's Steam launcher wrapper, for images that carry their own Steam.

SELKIES_RUN_AFTER_CONNECT.label: Run After Connect
SELKIES_RUN_AFTER_CONNECT.description: Shell command run inside the container when the first client connects.

SELKIES_RUN_AFTER_DISCONNECT.label: Run After Disconnect
SELKIES_RUN_AFTER_DISCONNECT.description: Shell command run inside the container when the last client disconnects.

SELKIES_APP_WAIT_READY.label: Wait for App Ready File
SELKIES_APP_WAIT_READY.description: Start streaming only once the ready file exists, for images whose sidecar signals when the application is up.

SELKIES_APP_READY_FILE.label: App Ready File
SELKIES_APP_READY_FILE.description: File the sidecar creates when the application is initialized.

SELKIES_AUDIT_WEBHOOK_URL.label: Audit Webhook URL
SELKIES_AUDIT_WEBHOOK_URL.description: Receives one JSON POST per clipboard transfer, file upload or download, printed document, page connection, and recording, with metadata only and never content. Empty sends nothing.

SELKIES_AUDIT_WEBHOOK_TOKEN.label: Audit Webhook Token
SELKIES_AUDIT_WEBHOOK_TOKEN.description: Bearer token sent in the Authorization header of every audit POST.

SELKIES_AUDIT_WEBHOOK_TIMEOUT.label: Audit Webhook Timeout (seconds)
SELKIES_AUDIT_WEBHOOK_TIMEOUT.description: Seconds one audit POST may take before it counts as failed and the next event is sent.

SELKIES_COMPUTER_USE_BIND.label: Computer-Use Server
SELKIES_COMPUTER_USE_BIND.description: Start pixelflux's Computer-Use HTTP server on these comma-separated entries: a bare port listens on loopback only, host:port names the address. Empty leaves it off. It starts only with the Computer-Use token.

SELKIES_COMPUTER_USE_TOKEN.label: Computer-Use Token
SELKIES_COMPUTER_USE_TOKEN.description: Bearer token every Computer-Use request has to carry in its Authorization header; the server does not start without one.

SELKIES_RECORDING_SOCKET.label: Recording Socket
SELKIES_RECORDING_SOCKET.description: Unix socket path of the out-of-band recording tap, which serves the video stream to connected recorders. Empty leaves it off.

SELKIES_DEBUG.label: Enable Selkies Debugging
SELKIES_DEBUG.description: Enable debug logging for streaming components.

SELKIES_MODE.label: Streaming Mode
SELKIES_MODE.description: Transport used by default. Auto picks WebRTC when any TURN/STUN value is set, otherwise WebSockets.

SELKIES_ENABLE_DUAL_MODE.label: Dual Mode
SELKIES_ENABLE_DUAL_MODE.description: Let users switch between WebRTC and WebSockets from the sidebar. Auto enables it only when WebRTC is configured.

SELKIES_WEBRTC_PACER.label: WebRTC Pacer
SELKIES_WEBRTC_PACER.description: Pace outgoing WebRTC packets with strict priorities so audio and input are protected from video bursts on congested links.

SELKIES_CONGESTION_CONTROL.label: Congestion Control
SELKIES_CONGESTION_CONTROL.description: Adapt the video bitrate to the bandwidth estimate from WebRTC receiver feedback. Effective in CBR mode.

SELKIES_WEBRTC_ICE_LITE.label: ICE-Lite
SELKIES_WEBRTC_ICE_LITE.description: Offer host candidates only and answer the client's connectivity checks, for a server whose addresses are reachable as advertised: a public IP, a static NAT with the public IP set, or forwarded mux ports.

SELKIES_WEBRTC_PORT_RANGE.label: UDP Port Range
SELKIES_WEBRTC_PORT_RANGE.description: Inclusive range, such as 50000-50100, that the sockets behind direct host candidates bind into, for deployments that allot each session a firewalled window. Empty uses ephemeral ports.

SELKIES_WEBRTC_UDP_MUX_PORT.label: UDP Mux Port
SELKIES_WEBRTC_UDP_MUX_PORT.description: One UDP port every session shares for its host candidates, so a single forwarded port serves any number of sessions. 0 gives each session sockets of its own.

SELKIES_WEBRTC_TCP_MUX_PORT.label: TCP Mux Port
SELKIES_WEBRTC_TCP_MUX_PORT.description: One TCP port accepting ICE-TCP connections for clients on networks that block UDP; 443 is the usual public choice. 0 offers no TCP candidates.

SELKIES_STUN_HOST.label: STUN Host
SELKIES_STUN_HOST.description: STUN server for NAT hole punching. Point at an internal server for networks without internet.

SELKIES_TURN_HOST.label: TURN Host
SELKIES_TURN_HOST.description: TURN server used with the shared secret or long-term credentials. Wrap IPv6 addresses in square brackets.

SELKIES_TURN_PROTOCOL.label: TURN Protocol
SELKIES_TURN_PROTOCOL.description: Transport the client uses to reach TURN. UDP is strongly recommended; use TCP only where UDP is blocked.

SELKIES_TURN_TLS.label: TURN over TLS/DTLS
SELKIES_TURN_TLS.description: Use TURN over TLS (TCP) or DTLS (UDP). Requires a valid certificate on the TURN server.

SELKIES_TURN_SHARED_SECRET.label: TURN Shared Secret
SELKIES_TURN_SHARED_SECRET.description: Shared secret used to generate time-limited HMAC TURN credentials.

SELKIES_TURN_REST_URI.label: TURN REST API URI
SELKIES_TURN_REST_URI.description: URI of a TURN REST credential service, e.g. http://localhost:8008.

SELKIES_TURN_REST_API_KEY.label: TURN REST API Key
SELKIES_TURN_REST_API_KEY.description: API key sent to the TURN REST service.

SELKIES_TURN_REST_USERNAME.label: TURN REST Username
SELKIES_TURN_REST_USERNAME.description: Username the TURN REST service embeds in the credential. Empty uses 'selkies'.

SELKIES_TURN_REST_USERNAME_AUTH_HEADER.label: TURN REST Username Header
SELKIES_TURN_REST_USERNAME_AUTH_HEADER.description: Header that carries the user name to the TURN REST service.

SELKIES_TURN_REST_PROTOCOL_HEADER.label: TURN REST Protocol Header
SELKIES_TURN_REST_PROTOCOL_HEADER.description: Header that carries the desired TURN transport protocol to the TURN REST service.

SELKIES_TURN_REST_TLS_HEADER.label: TURN REST TLS Header
SELKIES_TURN_REST_TLS_HEADER.description: Header that carries the TURN TLS choice to the TURN REST service.

SELKIES_WEBRTC_PUBLIC_IP.label: WebRTC Public IP
SELKIES_WEBRTC_PUBLIC_IP.description: Public address to advertise in host ICE candidates for a server behind static 1:1 NAT. One IPv4 and/or one IPv6 address.

SELKIES_ENABLE_CLOUDFLARE_TURN.label: Enable Cloudflare TURN
SELKIES_ENABLE_CLOUDFLARE_TURN.description: Use the Cloudflare TURN service. Requires the token ID and API token below.

SELKIES_CLOUDFLARE_TURN_TOKEN_ID.label: Cloudflare TURN Token ID
SELKIES_CLOUDFLARE_TURN_TOKEN_ID.description: The Cloudflare TURN app token ID.

SELKIES_RTC_CONFIG_JSON.label: RTC Config JSON Path
SELKIES_RTC_CONFIG_JSON.description: Path inside the container to a JSON file with the WebRTC configuration. Overrides every other STUN/TURN setting and is re-read periodically.

SELKIES_ENABLE_WEBRTC_STATISTICS.label: Dump WebRTC Statistics
SELKIES_ENABLE_WEBRTC_STATISTICS.description: Write the client's WebRTC statistics as CSV files under /tmp in the container, for diagnosis.

DOCKER_PRIVILEGED.label: Privileged Mode
DOCKER_PRIVILEGED.description: Give all caps to container, lift cgroup restrictions, mounts all host devices. This will break things!

DOCKER_ENV.label: Environment Variables
DOCKER_ENV.description: Extra environment variables (comma separated, e.g., KEY=VALUE,KEY2=VALUE2).

DOCKER_CAP_ADD.label: Cap Add
DOCKER_CAP_ADD.description: Add kernel capabilities (comma separated, e.g., SYS_ADMIN,MKNOD).

DOCKER_NANO_CPUS.label: Nano CPUs
DOCKER_NANO_CPUS.description: CPU quota in units of 1e-9 CPUs.

DOCKER_IPC_MODE.label: IPC Mode
DOCKER_IPC_MODE.description: Set the IPC mode for the container.

DOCKER_PID_MODE.label: PID Mode
DOCKER_PID_MODE.description: Set the PID mode for the container.

DOCKER_EXTRA_HOSTS.label: Extra Hosts
DOCKER_EXTRA_HOSTS.description: Host to IP mappings (comma separated, e.g., hostname:1.2.3.4).

DOCKER_GROUP_ADD.label: Group Add
DOCKER_GROUP_ADD.description: List of additional group names and/or IDs (comma separated).

appLaboratory.title: App Laboratory
appLaboratory.description: Create and test custom application configurations by layering changes on top of a base app.
appLaboratory.baseAppDescription: The installed application that your new custom app will be based on.
appLaboratory.placeholder: The App Labratory allows you to configure the base home directory and launch script for an application based on an existing installed application. This home directory will be copied on first init for the user with all files and settings you setup in this session. You can re-launch an existing Labratory App to modify it's contents further.
appLaboratory.formInvalid: Please select a base app and provide a name for the new app.
appLaboratory.explainer: The App Laboratory builds a meta-app: a variant of an installed application with its own name, icon, autostart script, and a home directory that is already set up. You set the application up once in a customization session, and every user's first launch starts from a copy of that home directory.
appLaboratory.step1: Pick the application to build on, and give the meta-app a name, an icon, and the users who may launch it.
appLaboratory.step2Title: Customize it in a live session
appLaboratory.step2: A customization session opens with the template home directory writable. Install extensions, sign in, arrange it as users should find it.
appLaboratory.step3Title: Close the session to save the template
appLaboratory.step3: Closing the session from this page keeps the home directory as the template.
appLaboratory.openDescription: Everything changed in this session's home directory becomes the template. The session stays open until you close it here; it is not listed among your sessions.
appLaboratory.confirmClose: Close the customization session of '{name}'? The session stops, and its home directory is kept as the template.
appLaboratory.unsavedClose: The changes could not be saved. Close the session anyway?
appLaboratory.templateSaved: Session closed. The template is saved.
appLaboratory.busy: A customization session for '{name}' is open. Close it above before changing a meta-app or starting another.
appLaboratory.customizeDescription: The customization session starts with these options. One session can be open at a time.

web.pickHelp: Drag this one there too. Click it, then click a link to open that link in SealSkin, or an image, video, or audio to send the file. Shift-click a link to send the file it leads to, fetched with your sign-in on that site.

cluster.confirmRemove: Remove node '{name}' from the cluster? A node that is still running registers again and waits for approval.
cluster.joinDescription: Create a join code, start the new node with the two lines below in its environment, then approve it in the table above. A code admits one node and lasts an hour.
cluster.joinExpires: Environment of the new node (the code expires {when})
cluster.poolsDescription: A pool is a set of nodes sessions start on. A restricted pool is open only to the users and groups named here or allowed by their settings.
cluster.poolDomainLabel: Domain the pool's nodes are named under
cluster.poolCostLabel: Allowance an hour of session costs
cluster.poolGpuCostLabel: Allowance an hour of GPU session costs (blank: the same)
cluster.poolUsersLabel: Users it is open to when restricted (comma-separated)
cluster.poolGroupsLabel: Groups it is open to when restricted (comma-separated)
cluster.poolStopWhenSpent: End sessions when the allowance is spent
cluster.storeDescription: Where the nodes keep the records they share: users, groups, apps, pools, and these settings.
cluster.sessionDomainUnset: Not set (the web app's host name)
cluster.sessionDomainOff: Off: sessions open on the web app's address
cluster.signInDescription: Written here, a setting holds for every node and takes precedence over a node's environment. Clear a field to hand the setting back to each node's environment.
cluster.settingFromEnvironment: From each node's environment; the value shown is this node's.
cluster.secretSet: A secret is set; leave blank to keep it

settings.saml_groups_attribute: SAML attribute listing the user's groups (empty: the groups claim below)

settings.sso_groups_claim: Claim or attribute listing the user's groups

settings.sso_force_login: Ask for credentials at every sign-in
settings.sso_create_users: Create a user at the first sign-in

settings.proxy_auth_groups_header: Header a trusted proxy lists the user's groups in

signin.providerHelp: A provider only fills the hints below; nothing about it is stored.
signin.proxyHelp: A reverse proxy in front signs users in and names them in a header. This suits a proxy that already guards your other sites the same way; otherwise sign users in above, over OpenID Connect or SAML.
signin.proxyPresetChoose: Choose the proxy's provider to fill the headers

reach.title: Reaching This Server
reach.help: How browsers reach this server, as the server and this browser see it. A reverse proxy in front has to get each of these right.
reach.publicUrlDiffers: This page was loaded from {origin}. Set SEALSKIN_PUBLIC_URL to the address browsers use: identity provider redirects are built from it.
reach.sessionNamesShared: Each session is a path of the web app, so no other name has to answer. SEALSKIN_SESSION_ISOLATION=true gives each a name of its own under the session domain.
reach.sessionNamesHelp: Launches from the web app will fail. A session opens on a name of its own, <session id>.<domain>: the domain needs wildcard DNS, a wildcard certificate, and a reverse proxy rule that sends those names here.
reach.sessionNamesGuarded: Sessions will open under {domain} as SEALSKIN_SESSION_DOMAIN says. That is expected when the reverse proxy asks for a sign-in on the session names; otherwise check the wildcard DNS, the certificate, and the proxy rule for them.
reach.sessionNamesOther: SEALSKIN_SESSION_DOMAIN names {domain}, which did not answer.
reach.viaOther: Not one of the trusted proxies. If this is your reverse proxy's address, add it to SEALSKIN_TRUSTED_PROXIES.
reach.viaDirect: No reverse proxy is trusted. If this is a reverse proxy's address, set SEALSKIN_TRUSTED_PROXIES to it, so the server sees each browser's own address.
reach.yourAddress: Your address, as the server sees it

authelia.name: Authelia
authelia.hint: The issuer is Authelia's own address, https://<host>. Add a client under identity_providers.oidc.clients with the redirect URI below, and the scopes openid profile groups email offline_access.

pocketid.name: Pocket ID
pocketid.hint: The issuer is Pocket ID's own address, https://<host>. Add an OIDC client with the callback URL below, and set the scopes to openid profile email groups.

tinyauth.name: Tinyauth
tinyauth.hint: The issuer is Tinyauth's own address, https://<host>. Define the client with the TINYAUTH_OIDC_CLIENTS_<NAME>_ variables, and set the scopes to openid profile email groups.

keycloak.name: Keycloak
keycloak.hint: The issuer is the realm's address, https://<host>/realms/<realm>. Create an OpenID Connect client with client authentication on, and add a group membership mapper named 'groups' to send the user's groups.

authentik.name: Authentik
authentik.hint: The issuer is the application's address, https://<host>/application/o/<slug>/, with its trailing slash. Create an OAuth2/OpenID provider and an application that uses it.

entra.name: Microsoft Entra ID
entra.hint: The issuer is https://login.microsoftonline.com/<tenant>/v2.0. Register an application, add a client secret, and add the groups claim under Token configuration.

google.name: Google
google.hint: The issuer is https://accounts.google.com. Create an OAuth client ID of type Web application. Google sends no groups.

okta.name: Okta
okta.hint: The issuer is your organization's address, https://<org>.okta.com. Create an OIDC web application and add a groups claim to its ID token.

other.name: Other
other.hint: The issuer is the address whose /.well-known/openid-configuration describes the provider.

signin.samlMetadata: Open this server's service provider metadata
signin.trustedProxiesHelp: Set on each node with SEALSKIN_TRUSTED_PROXIES. The header is believed only when the request comes from one of those addresses.
signin.noTrustedProxy: A user header is set, but this node trusts no proxy yet, so no proxy sign-in is accepted.

proxyCheck.guarded: Checked: the proxy does not pass on the sign-in headers a visitor sends.
proxyCheck.unreachable: Proxy sign-ins are refused: this node cannot check the proxy. Give it a route to its public URL, name the proxy's own address in SEALSKIN_TRUSTED_PROXIES, or set SEALSKIN_PROXY_AUTH_UNCHECKED=true on the node to believe the proxy without the check.
proxyCheck.unchecked: The check of the proxy is switched off on this node (SEALSKIN_PROXY_AUTH_UNCHECKED): whatever the proxy passes on is believed.

signin.whoHelp: These hold for OpenID Connect, SAML, and the reverse proxy. To put the members of an identity provider group into a SealSkin group, list it under "Identity provider groups" of that group in Groups.
signin.rootHelp: Always available. The token is in /config/root_token on the server until that file is deleted, and can be set with SEALSKIN_ROOT_TOKEN.
signin.keyOn: This node accepts the key-file clients: the browser extension and the mobile app. Set on each node with SEALSKIN_LEGACY_AUTH.
signin.keyOff: This node does not accept key-file clients. Set on each node with SEALSKIN_LEGACY_AUTH.
